Target_Spot shows small leaf spots only — doesn't match.

**Summary of analysis:**

The test image shows a tomato stem/petiole with a **long, narrow brown/reddish-brown longitudinal streak running along its surface**, with the epidermis appearing cracked/split open, while the rest of the stem remains green. No fungal mycelium is visible.

- Most fungal diseases (Sclerotinia, Southern Blight, Gray Mold, Late Blight, Phytophthora) showed either white mycelium, dark/black lesions, or crown-level collapse — ruled out.
- Wilt diseases (Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium) showed whole-plant wilting or internal vascular discoloration upon cutting — not matching.
- The Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato reference included stem images showing longitudinal brown discoloration consistent with how bacterial canker opens/cracks the stem tissue. Image number 1573932 from the same Bugwood series appeared in that class's reference, suggesting proximity to the test image (1573600).
- Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus showed one stem reference with brown streaking, but TSWV primarily manifests as ring spots on leaves/fruit.

The elongated surface canker with longitudinal cracking on a green stem is the hallmark of **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato** (*Clavibacter michiganensis*).
